annotation.title_clean: Guidelines for the use of AI systems in courts and tribunals
annotation.title_en: Guidelines for the use of AI systems in courts and tribunals
annotation.summary_en: UNESCO publication page for its 2025 Guidelines for the Use of AI Systems in Courts and Tribunals. The page describes the first global ethical and operational framework for AI in the judiciary. It sets out fifteen universal principles, presents AI as an assistive rather than a substitute tool under meaningful human supervision, and comes with a capacity-building toolkit.
key_provisions_or_claims: Fifteen universal principles guide the adoption, governance and oversight of AI in the judiciary
AI should assist judges, not replace them, and always operate under meaningful human supervision
Principles include transparency, accountability, human oversight, human rights protection and multistakeholder governance
Developed through consultations with experts from over 160 countries and more than 36,000 judicial actors
Comes with a capacity-building toolkit for judges, court administrators and policymakers
